comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose strategic initiatives to optimize software and frameworks for AI workloads, though they focus on different layers of the stack. AVGO describes Tanzu Data as a suite providing advanced analytical data warehouse capabilities and vector database capabilities specifically for AI use cases, focusing on the data access and management layer. In contrast, INTC focuses on the hardware-software co-optimization layer, stating it aims to optimize AI frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow to run efficiently on its hardware, and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. While AVGO provides the data infrastructure for AI applications, INTC provides the optimization tools to accelerate AI inference on its processors.

sentences.text: • Tanzu Data: A suite of data services that provides advanced analytical data warehouse capabilities and real-time transactions and processing at massive scale with an in-memory data grid with vector database capabilities for AI use cases.
We aim to optimize AI frameworks and middleware, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, Hugging Face and WebNN to run efficiently on our hardware.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel launched a suite of edge computing processors including the Intel Core Ultra 200S Series, which integrates NPU IP into desktops to reduce package power while utilizing advanced performance and power-efficient cores with the latest packaging technology.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC highlight the integration of specialized AI processing capabilities into their respective product suites for broader computing platforms. AVGO's Tanzu Data includes an in-memory data grid with vector database capabilities to support AI use cases, enabling real-time data access for AI applications. Similarly, INTC describes launching edge computing processors, specifically the Intel Core Ultra 200S Series, which brings NPU (Neural Processing Unit) IP to desktops to handle AI workloads. AVGO addresses AI through software-defined data services and grids, whereas INTC addresses it through hardware integration of NPUs into its processor suite for edge and desktop applications.
